standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Etale Cohomology, proposition etale-cohomology-proposition-finite-higher-direct-image-zero (invoked at proof line 538)
standard_prerequisites.use: After the reduction to schemes it identifies the stalk of the pushforward with the product of the stalks at the finitely many lifts.

core_obligations: Choose an etale neighbourhood $(V, \overline{v})$ of the geometric point $\overline{y}$ and note that the stalk of $f_*\mathcal{F}$ at $\overline{y}$ is the stalk of $f_*\mathcal{F}|_V$ at $\overline{v}$ (proof lines 531-533).
Use the base change statement for pushforwards to replace $Y$ by $V$ and $X$ by $X \times_Y V$, so that the morphism becomes a finite morphism of schemes (proof lines 534-537).
Apply the corresponding statement in etale cohomology of schemes to conclude that the stalk is the product of the stalks at the lifts $\overline{x}_1, \ldots, \overline{x}_n$ (proof lines 537-539).
proof_roadmap: Passing to an etale neighbourhood (proof lines 531-533).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the stalk of the pushforward of a sheaf along a finite morphism at a geometric point as the product of the stalks over the finitely many lifts of that point (statement lines 517-528, tag 0DK3). The proof passes to an etale neighbourhood of the geometric point, uses the base change description of pushforwards to reduce to a finite morphism of schemes, and applies the known scheme statement there. The reduction through the etale neighbourhood is the substance, so the claim is H2.
